## Allow Multiple Memberships

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/allow-multiple-memberships>

Allow Multiple Memberships | User Registration & Membership

# Allow Multiple Memberships
Pro Learn how to enable users to purchase and hold multiple membership plans simultaneously using Membership Groups, allowing flexible combinations of access levels and benefits.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to let your members purchase and hold more than one membership plan at the same time? User Registration & Membership allows you to enable multiple memberships through Membership Groups, giving your members the flexibility to combine different access levels and benefits.

This tutorial will show you how to set up and manage multiple memberships for your site.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the **User Registration & Membership** plugin. Then, make sure you've installed and activated User Registration & Membership Pro with a Plus or Professional license, as the multiple memberships feature requires a premium plan.

## Understanding Multiple Memberships (Pro)

Multiple memberships allow a single user to purchase and maintain more than one active membership plan simultaneously. Each membership operates independently with its own:

Billing cycle and renewal schedule

Access permissions and content restrictions

Subscription status and payment history

For example, a member could hold both a "Basic Content Access" membership and a "Premium Course Bundle" membership at the same time, gaining the combined benefits of both plans.

Multiple memberships must be configured through Membership Groups. You cannot enable this feature on individual membership plans.

## Creating a Membership Group

To enable multiple memberships, you first need to create a Membership Group that contains the plans you want to offer together.

From your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership → Groups**.

On the Groups page, click **Add New** in the top-right corner.

Configure your group settings:

Enter a **Group Name** (for example, "Content & Courses Bundle")

Add a **Group Description** explaining what memberships are included

From the **Select Memberships** dropdown, choose which membership plans to include in this group

Click on the toggle button and enable **Enable multiple membership.**

Click **Publish** to create the group

You cannot enable Allow Multiple Memberships and Upgrade Action at the same time within a single group. These features are mutually exclusive — choose the one that fits your business model.

## How Members Purchase Multiple Memberships

When multiple memberships are enabled, the purchase process works differently than standard single-membership registration.

Members cannot select multiple memberships during their initial registration. Instead, they must:

Register and purchase their first membership through the normal registration process

Log in to their account after completing the first purchase

Navigate to the membership listing page or their account dashboard

Purchase additional memberships from the same group

Each membership requires a separate checkout process. Members will complete individual transactions for each plan they want to add to their account.

## Using the Buy Now Button Block

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/buy-now>

Add Membership Buy Now Buttons in WordPress | URM Docs

# Using the Buy Now Button Block
Add membership purchase buttons anywhere on your WordPress site to enable instant checkout for your membership plans using the Buy Now Button Block.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

Would you like to add a quick purchase button for your membership plans directly on any page or post? User Registration & Membership allows you to place membership purchase buttons anywhere on your site using the Buy Now Button Block.

This guide will show you how to add and customize these buttons so visitors can instantly start the checkout process for your membership plans.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the **User Registration & Membership plugin** on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've created at least one membership plan that you want to sell.

## Adding the Buy Now Button to Your Page

To add a Buy Now button, go to the page or post where you want the button to appear.

Click the **+** button in the top-left corner of the WordPress editor to open the block inserter.

Search for **Membership Buy Now** in the block list.

Click the block to insert it into your content.

Once you've added the block, you'll see the button appear on your page with default settings. Now you can customize it to match your needs.

## Selecting Your Membership Plan

After adding the block, look at the block settings panel on the right side of your screen.

In the **General** tab, you'll see a **Membership Plan** dropdown. Click this dropdown and select which membership plan you want this button to link to.

When visitors click this button, they'll be redirected directly to the checkout page for the membership plan you selected here.

## Customizing the Button Text

By default, the button displays generic text like "Buy Now." You can change this to anything that fits your site.

In the block settings, find the **Button Text** field. Enter your custom text here—for example, "Get Access," "Upgrade to Silver," or "Join Now."

The text you enter will immediately appear on the button in the editor preview.

## Adjusting Button Width and Alignment

You can control how wide the button appears and where it sits on the page.

In the block settings, find the **Width** option. You can choose from:

**25%** — Quarter width

**50%** — Half width

**75%** — Three-quarter width

**100%** — Full width

Next, use the **Justification** setting to align the button:

**Left** — Button aligns to the left side

**Center** — Button centers on the page

**Right** — Button aligns to the right side

These settings help you create the exact layout you need, whether you want a small centered button or a full-width call-to-action.

## Choosing a Button Style

The block offers two visual styles for your button.

In the **Styles** tab of the block settings, you'll see:

**Fill** — Creates a solid background button with your chosen colors

**Outline** — Creates a bordered button with a transparent background

Select the style that best matches your site's design.

## Customizing Button Colors

You can fully customize the button's appearance to match your branding.

In the **Color** section of the block settings, you'll find four color options:

**Text Color** — Changes the color of the button text

**Background Color** — Sets the button's background color

**Text Hover Color** — Changes text color when visitors hover over the button

**Background Hover Color** — Changes background color on hover

Click each color picker to select your preferred colors. The button preview updates in real-time as you make changes.

## Adjusting Typography and Size

To change the button text size, go to the **Typography** section in the block settings.

You can choose from four preset sizes:

**S** — Small

**M** — Medium

**L** — Large

**XL** — Extra Large

Select the size that provides the best readability and visual impact for your design.

## Configuring Border Settings

You can add or customize the button's border to create different visual effects.

In the **Border** section, you'll find:

**Border Color** — Sets the color of the button's border

**Border Thickness** — Controls how thick the border appears (measured in pixels)

For the **Border Radius** setting, enter a value in pixels to control corner roundness:

**0px** — Creates sharp, square corners

**Higher values** — Creates rounded corners (larger numbers create more rounded, pill-shaped buttons)

## Opening Checkout in a New Tab

If you're adding the button to a marketing page and want visitors to stay on your main content, you can make the checkout page open in a new browser tab.

In the block settings, find the **Open in New Tab** toggle and turn it on.

When enabled, clicking the button opens the checkout page in a new tab, keeping your original page open in the background.

## Creating a Free Membership Plan

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/creating-a-free-membership-plan>

Create Free Membership Site | User Registration & Membership

# Creating a Free Membership Plan
Learn how to set up a free membership plan to grant no-cost access to restricted content on your WordPress site.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

Would you like to create a membership website where users can register for free and access exclusive content? User Registration & Membership allows you to create free membership plans with content restrictions, so you can build a community site without charging for access. This tutorial will show you how to set up a free membership website from start to finish.

## Creating Free Membership in WordPress

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site.

### Step 1: Create New Membership

Log in to your WordPress dashboard

Navigate to User Registration & Membership → Memberships

Click the Add New button (or Create new Membership button)

### Step 2: Configure Basic Settings

On the Basics tab, configure the following:

Membership Name: Enter a clear name for your plan (e.g., "Free Member", "Basic Access")

Description: Add details about what this membership includes

Membership Type: Select **Free **from the option.

### Step 3: Configure Access Settings

Switch to the Access tab to control what content members can view:

Click the **Content.**

Select the type of content to restrict:

Pages: Choose specific pages members can access

Posts: Select individual posts

Whole site: Grant access to your entire site

Custom post types: Restrict custom content types (Pro only)

Menu items: Control menu visibility (Pro only)

Taxonomies: Restrict by categories or tags (Pro only)

After selecting content type, choose the specific items like pages, posts, media.

Configure the Restriction Message that non-members will see when trying to access protected content.

### Step 4: Configure Advanced Settings (Optional)

Cn the Advanced tab, you can optionally configure:

Trial Period: Not applicable for free memberships

Upgrade Action: Enable if you want members to upgrade to paid plans later. Select which plan to go after the free plan.

Email Marketing Override: Override form-level email marketing settings if needed

### Step 5: Save Your Membership Plan

Click **Publish** (or Save Changes if editing) to publish your free membership plan.

## Add the Membership to a Registration Form

After creating your membership plan, add it to a registration form:

Go to User Registration & Membership → Registration Forms

Select an existing form, but if you have no forms created, the default form will open.

In the form builder, search for Membership Field in the left panel

Drag the Membership Field into your form

Click on the field to configure options: Choose Show all active memberships or Select a group

Click Update Form to save the changes.

## Testing Your Free Membership Site

Before launching your membership site, test the complete user experience. Open your site in an incognito or private browser window to simulate a new visitor.

Navigate to your registration page and fill out the form with test information. Use a real email address you can access so you can verify any confirmation emails.

After submitting the registration form, check that you're redirected to the appropriate page. By default, users are redirected to the My Account page after registration.

Try accessing a restricted page while logged in as your test user. Verify that you can view the protected content. Then, log out and try accessing the same page again—you should see the restriction message instead of the content.

Test the login process by visiting your login page and signing in with your test account credentials. Verify that you're redirected to the correct page after login.

## Creating a Recurring Subscription Membership Plan

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/creating-a-recurring-subscription-membership>

Create Recurring Subscription Membership Plans in WordPress

# Creating a Recurring Subscription Membership Plan
Learn how to set up automated recurring subscription plans or paid membership plan with payment gateways, trial periods, and membership upgrades using User Registration & Membership Pro.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Want to charge members on a recurring basis for premium content? User Registration & Membership lets you create subscription plans with automatic billing. This tutorial shows you how to set up a subscription membership plan with payment gateways, trial periods, and upgrade options.

Before getting started, make sure you have installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. You will also need a payment gateway account such as PayPal or Stripe to process recurring payments.

## Creating Your Subscription Membership Plan

To create a new subscription membership plan, go to User Registration & Membership > Memberships. Here, you will see a list of all your existing membership plans.

Click the Create new Membership button in the top-right corner. This will open the membership creation screen where you can configure all the details for your subscription plan.

## Configuring Basic Membership Details

In the Basics tab, start by entering a Membership Name that clearly describes your plan. This name will be visible to users when they choose a membership tier.

Add a Membership Description to explain what members get with this plan. Include details about the features, content access, or benefits they will receive.

Set the Membership Status to Enable so the plan is active and available to users. You can disable it later if you need to pause new signups.

## Setting Up Subscription Pricing

Under Membership **Type**, select Subscription-Based. This enables recurring billing for the membership plan.

Enter the regular payment amount in the Price field. This is what members will be charged for each billing cycle.

Set the Billing Cycle to define how often members are charged. You can choose from daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom intervals. For example, selecting monthly means members will be billed every month.

Select **One-Time Payment** if you only want a single payment for your membership plan.

## Managing User Access

Click on the Access tab, and manage your access control for the membership.

Click on +**Content** on the Access tab and select the page, posts, other types, or the whole site to be restricted. If you choose pages, or posts, further select specific pages that you want to provide access to this membership owners.

For more specific restrictions, you can do so from the Content Rules page.

You can also set the restriction message shown to non members, either global or custom message for that specific plan.

## Assigning User Roles

In the Advanced tab, select the Membership Role from the dropdown. This is the WordPress user role that will be assigned to members when they subscribe to this plan.

The role determines what permissions members have on your site beyond the content restrictions you set up.

## Adding a Trial Period

If you want to offer a trial period, toggle on the Trial Period option in the **Advanced tab**. This allows users to subscribe without payment for an allocated trial duration.

Set the Trial Duration to specify how long the trial lasts. You can configure this in days, weeks, months, or years.

During the trial period, members have full access to the membership benefits. Once the trial ends, they will be automatically charged according to your billing cycle.

Then, click on **Publish**. We'll have to get back once, we setup the payment options.

## Configuring Payment Gateways

Before enabling payment gateways on your membership plan, you need to configure them in the global settings. Go to User Registration & Membership > Settings > Payments.

### Setting Up Stripe

Click the Stripe dropdown menu. Enter your Publishable Key and Secret Key if you want to test payments first. Toggle Enable Test Mode to on.

When you are ready to accept real payments, enter your Live Publishable Key and Live Secret Key, then toggle Enable Test Mode to off.

For Stripe subscriptions to work properly, you must set up webhooks. Log into your Stripe Dashboard, search for Developers, and click Webhooks. Click Add Destination, select the invoice events, and enter your webhook URL in this format: yoursite.com/wp-json/user-registration/stripe-webhook. Click Add Endpoint to save.

### Setting Up PayPal

Click the PayPal dropdown menu. Select Mode as either Sandbox for testing or Production for live payments.

Enter your PayPal Email address that will receive payments. Add a Cancel URL where users are redirected if they cancel payment, and a Return URL where they go after successful payment.

Enter your Client ID and Client Secret from your PayPal Developer Dashboard. Click Save Changes.

## Enabling Payment Gateways on Your Membership

After you setup your payment gateways, users can choose either of these (plus more) two methods during the membership purchase/registration.

## Setting Up Membership Upgrades

Let's go back to **Memberships** and click on **Edit **for the membership you just created.

If you want members to upgrade from this plan to a higher tier, toggle on the **Upgrade Action** option in the Advanced tab.

Click in the Upgrade Path field and select which membership plans this plan can upgrade to. You can select multiple upgrade options.

Choose the upgrade pricing model. Full Amount Upgrade charges the complete price of the new plan. Proration Upgrade calculates the difference based on remaining subscription time, so members only pay for the unused portion.

## Saving Your Membership Plan

Once you have configured all the settings, click the **Save/Publish** button in the top-right corner to save your subscription plan.

Your subscription membership plan is now active and ready to accept recurring payments from members.

## Adding the Membership to a Registration Form

To allow users to sign up for your subscription plan, you need to add it to a registration form. Go to User Registration & Membership > All Forms > Registration Forms.

Select an existing form or create a new one. In the form builder, search for Membership Field in the left panel and drag it into your form.

Click on the Membership Field to configure its options.

Under **Membership Display Options**, choose Show all active memberships to display all your plans, or Select a group if you have organized memberships into groups.

Click Update Form to save your changes. Users who fill out this form will now see your subscription plan as an option during registration.

## Setting Up Registration and Other Pages

By default User Registration and Membership adds necessary new pages on your website like My Account page, signup page, Pricing page etc. But, you can manually assign these pages as well.

Go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > General > Pages** to configure where users go during and after registration.

Assign the Pages from the dropdown, if you prefer. This is where members are redirected after successfully completing payment and registration.

Click **Save Changes**. Your subscription membership system is now fully configured.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I offer both monthly and yearly subscription options?

Yes. Create separate membership plans for each billing cycle. For example, create one plan with a monthly billing cycle and another with a yearly billing cycle. Both can provide access to the same content but with different pricing and renewal schedules.

### What happens when a subscription payment fails?

User Registration & Membership includes smart payment recovery that automatically retries failed payments and sends reminder emails to members. You can configure retry attempts and email notifications in the payment settings.

### Can members cancel their subscriptions?

Yes. Members can cancel their subscriptions from the Payment Details tab in their account dashboard. They can choose to cancel at the end of the current billing cycle or cancel immediately. If they cancel at the end of the billing cycle, they can reactivate the subscription before it expires.

### How do I restrict content to subscription members only?

Go to the Access tab when editing your membership plan. Click the Content dropdown and select the pages, posts, or content types you want to restrict. Only members with an active subscription to this plan will be able to access the restricted content.

That's it! Now you know how to create a recurring subscription membership plan with User Registration & Membership Pro. Next, would you like to learn how to restrict content to your subscription members? Be sure to check out our guide on content restriction for all the details.

## Creating Membership Groups

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/creating-membership-groups>

Creating Membership Groups

# Creating Membership Groups
Learn how to organize membership plans into logical groups using the User Registration & Membership plugin for improved management and user experience.
Last updated on Jul 17, 2026

Would you like to organize your membership plans into logical groups for easier management and better user experience?

User Registration & Membership allows you to bundle related membership plans together using Membership Groups. This guide will show you how to create and configure membership groups to organize your plans effectively.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've created at least one membership plan that you want to add to a group.

## Creating Your First Membership Group

Go to the Groups page by **User Registration & Membership > Group, and** click the **Add New** button to create a new membership group. This will open the group creation interface where you can configure your group settings.

## Configuring Basic Group Settings

In the group creation screen, you'll need to configure three essential settings:

**Group Name**: Enter a descriptive name for your membership group. For example, if you're bundling coding-related memberships, you might name it "Aspiring Coders" or "Developer Plans."

**Group Description**: Add a description that explains the purpose of this group and what memberships it includes. This helps you remember why you created the group and what it's meant to accomplish.

**Select Memberships**: From the dropdown menu, select which membership plans you want to include in this group. You can add multiple plans to a single group.

Once you've configured these settings, click **Publish** to create your membership group.

## Displaying Membership Groups on Your Site

After creating your group, you can display it on your website in two ways:

**Using a Shortcode**: Go to **User Registration & Memberships → Groups**, locate your group in the list, and copy the shortcode from the Shortcode column. The shortcode format is `[user_registration_groups id="X"]` where X is your group ID.

Paste this shortcode into any page or post where you want the group to appear.

**Using the Membership Pricing Block**: In the WordPress block editor, add the Membership Pricing block to your page.

In the block settings, you can choose to display specific membership groups instead of all memberships.

## Advanced Group Features (Plus/Professional Plans)

If you have a Plus or Professional license, you can access two advanced features that change how membership groups function:

### Allow Multiple Memberships

Enable the **Allow Multiple Memberships** toggle to let users purchase more than one plan from the group simultaneously.

Users cannot select multiple memberships during registration—they must register first, purchase their first membership, then log in to purchase additional plans from the group.

### Upgrade Action

Enable the **Upgrade Action** toggle to allow users to upgrade from one plan to another within the group. When you enable this feature, you'll need to configure two additional settings:

**Upgrade Type**: Choose between Full Amount Upgrade (users pay the full price difference between plans) or Proration Upgrade (users pay only the difference based on remaining time in their current subscription).

**Upgrade Path Order**: Define the sequential order users can upgrade through plans by arranging them from top to bottom. For example, you might set up Silver → Gold → Platinum. Users can only upgrade to the next plan in the sequence while their current membership is active.

You cannot enable Allow Multiple Memberships and Upgrade Action simultaneously within a single group—these features conflict with each other.

## Creating Memberships with a Free Trial

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/creating-memberships-with-a-free-trial>

How to Create Memberships with Free Trials in WordPress

# Creating Memberships with a Free Trial
Learn how to set up subscription-based memberships with free trial periods, allowing users to access content before committing to payment.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Want to let potential members try your content before they commit to paying? User Registration & Membership allows you to offer free trial periods on subscription-based memberships, giving users full access without any upfront charges. This guide will walk you through setting up memberships with trial periods.

**Requirements:** This feature requires the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin (Personal plan or higher).

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've configured at least one payment gateway (Stripe or PayPal) in your payment settings.

## Creating a Membership Plan with a Trial Period

To create a membership with a free trial, go to **User Registration & Membership → Memberships** and click **Add New**.

Here, you'll see the membership creation form with three main tabs: Basics, Access, and Advanced.

### Configuring Basic Membership Settings

In the **Basics** tab, configure your membership plan details:

Enter a **Membership Name** (for example, "Premium Monthly")

Add a **Membership Description** explaining what the membership includes

Set **Membership Status** to **Enable**

Select **Subscription-Based** as the **Membership Type** (trial periods only work with subscription memberships)

Enter the **Amount** members will pay after the trial ends

Set the **Billing Cycle** (for example, "1 month" for monthly subscriptions)

You need to enable a payment Gateway to accept payments from global settings.

### Enabling the Trial Period

Once you've configured the basic settings, scroll down to the **Advanced** tab.

In the Advanced tab, you'll find the **Trial Period** option. Toggle this setting to **Yes**.

When you enable the trial period, two new fields appear:

**Trial Duration Value**: Enter the number of time units (for example, "7" for a 7-day trial)

**Trial Duration Unit**: Select the time unit from the dropdown (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years)

For example, to offer a 14-day free trial, enter "14" in the Trial Duration Value field and select "Days" from the Trial Duration Unit dropdown.

### How Trial Periods Work

Once you've configured the trial period, here's what happens when a user signs up:

The user completes the registration form and selects your membership plan

They enter their payment information (required even for trials)

They get immediate access to all membership content

No payment is charged during the trial period

After the trial ends, the first payment is automatically processed

The subscription continues with regular billing cycles

Users must provide valid payment information during signup, even though they won't be charged until the trial ends. This ensures a smooth transition to paid membership when the trial period expires.

## Setting Up Content Access

After configuring the trial period, go to the **Access** tab to define what content trial members can access.

Click **+ Content** and select the content type you want to restrict (for example, **Selected pages** or **Specific posts**). Then, choose which pages or posts trial members can view.

Trial members have the same access as paid members during the trial period. Once the trial ends and payment is processed, their access continues without interruption.

## Publishing Your Membership Plan

Once you've configured all settings, click **Create Membership** to save your plan.

Your membership with a free trial is now active. Users can sign up through your registration form and start their trial immediately.

## Member Directory

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/member-directory>

Member Directory Setup Guide for WordPress Users

# Member Directory
Pro Create a searchable, customizable frontend directory to display registered user profiles with filtering and search capabilities using the Member Directory addon.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to create a searchable directory of your registered users on your website? User Registration & Membership allows you to display user profiles in a customizable frontend directory with filtering, search, and profile viewing capabilities.

This tutorial will show you how to set up and configure a member directory on your WordPress site.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've installed and activated the Member Directory addon, which is available with Personal, Plus, Professional, and ThemeGrill Agency plans.

## Enabling the Member Directory Addon

To create a member directory, you'll first need to enable the Member Directory addon.

From your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership → Addons**. Here, you'll see a list of available addons organized by category.

Locate **Members Directory** under the User Management section. Toggle the switch to activate the addon.

Once activated, you'll see a new **Members Directory** menu item in your User Registration & Membership section.

## Creating Your First Member Directory

Now you're ready to create your first member directory listing.

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Members Directory** and click the **Add New** button at the top of the page.

Enter a title for your directory. This title is for internal reference only — visitors won't see it on the frontend.

## Configuring General Settings

The General tab controls the basic display and behavior of your member directory.

### Choosing Which Users to Display

In the **Show users based on** dropdown, select which users should appear in your directory:

**All Users** — Displays all registered WordPress users

**Memberships** — Shows only users with specific membership levels

**Forms** — Displays only users who registered through specific User Registration forms

If you select **Memberships** or **Forms**, additional options will appear where you can choose which specific memberships or forms to include.

### Enabling Profile Pages

Toggle on **Enable view profile** if you want visitors to be able to click on user cards and view detailed profile pages. When enabled, you can customize the **View profile button text** (the default is "View Profile").

### Selecting the Layout

Choose your **Listings Layout**:

**List** — Displays users in a vertical list format

**Grid** — Shows users as cards in a grid layout

### Choosing Which Information to Display

In the **Select info to show in cards** section, choose which user fields should appear on each user's directory card. You can select multiple fields like First Name, Last Name, Email, Bio, or any custom fields you've added to your registration forms.

Toggle on **Enable Profile Picture** if you want user profile photos to appear in the directory cards.

## Configuring Profile Page Settings

If you enabled profile viewing in the General tab, the Profile Page tab lets you control what information appears on individual user profile pages.

Click the **Profile Page** tab to access these settings.

Here, you'll see a list of available user fields. Select which fields should appear on profile pages by checking the boxes next to each field.

You can reorder fields by dragging them up or down. To remove a field, click the **×** button next to it.

Now, you can view the profiles.

## Configuring Advanced Settings

The Advanced tab provides powerful filtering, search, and pagination options for your directory.

### Setting Up Sorting Options

Toggle on **Display Sorter** to add a sorting dropdown to your directory. This allows visitors to sort users by:

Latest registration date

First name

Last name

Display name

In the **Default User Sorter** dropdown, choose how users should be sorted when visitors first view the directory.

### Restricting by Role or Status

Use **Restrict By Role** to hide specific user roles from the directory. For example, you might want to hide Administrators or Editors from public view.

In **Select User Status**, choose which user approval statuses should be visible in the directory (Approved, Pending, Denied, or Awaiting Email Confirmation).

### Enabling Search Functionality

Toggle on **Display search form** to add a search box above your directory.

In **Search User According To**, select which fields visitors can search by. You can choose multiple fields like First Name, Last Name, Email, or custom fields.

### Adding Advanced Filters

Toggle on **Display Advanced Filter** to enable advanced filtering options for visitors.

In the **Advanced Filter** section, select which form fields should be available as filters. You can add custom fields by selecting **Other (Custom Field)** and entering the field name as the Meta Key.

Advanced filters only work with meta fields, not standard user table fields.

### Configuring Pagination

Toggle on **Display Amount Filter** to let visitors choose how many profiles to display per page (10, 20, 50, or 100).

In **Default number of profiles per page**, set how many user profiles appear on each page when visitors first view the directory.

## Publishing Your Member Directory

Once you've configured all your settings, click **Save** or **Publish** to save your directory configuration.

After saving, you'll see a shortcode at the top of the page that looks like this:

Text JavaScript TypeScript JSX TSX JSON PHP Python Bash HTML CSS SCSS SQL YAML Markdown Go Java Ruby Rust
`[user_registration_frontend_list id="123"]`

Copy this shortcode.

## Adding the Directory to Your Website

Now you're ready to display your member directory on your website.

### Using the Shortcode

Create a new page or edit an existing one where you want the directory to appear. Add a **Shortcode** block to the page and paste your directory shortcode.

Click **Update** or **Publish** to make your directory live.

### Using the Block Editor

Alternatively, you can use the **User Registration Membership Directory** block. In the block editor, click the **+** icon to add a new block, then search for "User Registration Frontend Listing."

Select the block and choose your directory from the dropdown in the block settings.

## Testing Your Member Directory

Visit the page where you added your directory to see it in action. You should see:

User cards or list items displaying the fields you selected

Profile pictures (if enabled)

Search functionality (if enabled)

Sorting options (if enabled)

Advanced filters (if enabled)

Pagination controls (if enabled)

If you enabled profile viewing, click on a user card or the "View Profile" button to see the detailed profile page.

## Member Management

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/member-management>

Member Management | User Registration & Membership Docs

# Member Management
Centralized dashboard for viewing, editing, and managing all users registered through User Registration forms, including member details, status control, and activity tracking.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to view, edit, and manage all users who have registered through your User Registration forms? User Registration & Membership provides a dedicated Members area where you can control user access, track activity, and manage member details—all from a centralized dashboard.

This tutorial will show you how to access the Members area, view member details, edit user information, manage user status, and track member activity.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. You'll also need administrator access to manage members, and at least one user registered through a User Registration form.

## Accessing the Members Area

To access the Members area, go to **User Registration & Membership > Members** from your WordPress dashboard. Here, you'll see a list of all users who have registered through User Registration forms.

The Members table displays key information including member names, email addresses, registration dates, and current status. You can search for specific members, filter by membership plan or status, and perform bulk actions on multiple members at once.

## Viewing Member Details

To view detailed information about a specific member, hover over the user record in the Members table and click on the **Edit** button.

This opens the member details page, which displays:

Personal information including name, email, username, and profile details

Registration source and date

Current user status and role

Membership plan details (if applicable)

Entry details showing all form field submissions

The Entry Details section shows exactly what information the user submitted during registration, making it easy to review their application or verify their details.

## Editing Member Information

Once in edit mode, you can update user details including their name, email, username, and other profile information. If you need to reset their password, you can set a new password directly from this screen. Click **Save Changes **to save your changes.

## Managing User Status

User Registration & Membership extends WordPress's basic user management with additional status controls that let you manage access without deleting accounts or losing user data.

From the Members table or member details page, you can change a user's status to:

**Approve User** — Allows the user to access the site and use available features

**Deny User** — Restricts the user from accessing the site

**Enable User** — Activates the user account and restores access

**Disable User** — Temporarily disables or deactivates the user account and restricts access for a specified duration (days, weeks, months, or years)

**Delete User** — Permanently removes the user and all associated data from the site

To change a user's status, hover over their record in the Members table and select the desired action from the available options. For temporary restrictions, the Disable User option allows you to specify exactly how long the user should be restricted from accessing the site.

## Tracking User Activity with User Journey

User Registration & Membership Pro includes a User Journey feature that tracks member activities across your website. To enable this feature, go to **User Registration & Membership > Settings > Advanced > Others** and turn on the **Enable User Activity Tracker** option.

Once enabled, you can view the User Journey table inside the View User dashboard. This table shows:

Pages visited by the member

Time spent on each page

Form interactions and completion status

Navigation patterns before and after registration

The User Journey feature is only available with User Registration & Membership Pro. User Activity Tracker must be enabled in settings before User Journey data appears.

## Searching and Filtering Members

The Members area includes powerful search and filtering tools to help you find specific users quickly:

Use the search bar to find members by username or email address

Filter by membership plan to see all members on a specific tier

Filter by user status to view approved, pending, or denied members

Sort by registration date, name, or other columns by clicking the column headers

These filters help you segment your member base and perform targeted actions on specific groups of users.

## Performing Bulk Actions

To manage multiple members at once, select the checkboxes next to the user records you want to modify. Then, choose an action from the **Bulk actions** dropdown menu at the top of the table and click **Apply**.

Bulk actions allow you to efficiently manage large numbers of members without having to edit each account individually.

That's it! Now you know how to manage members in User Registration & Membership. Next, would you like to learn how to create membership plans or set up content restrictions? Be sure to check out our guide on creating membership plans for all the details.

---

## Membership Rules

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/membership-rules>

WordPress Membership Rules | User Registration & Membership

# Membership Rules
Control member access to WordPress content by creating rules that automatically restrict pages and posts based on membership plans and subscription levels.
Last updated on Jul 16, 2026

Would you like to control which members can access specific content on your WordPress site? User Registration & Membership allows you to create membership rules that restrict pages, posts, and other content based on membership plans. Once configured, access is granted or denied automatically based on each member's active subscription — no manual management required.

## Prerequisites

Before getting started, make sure you have:

Installed and activated the **User Registration & Membership** plugin on your WordPress site.

Created at least one membership plan. If you haven't done this yet, refer to the 👉 How to Create a Membership Plan guide first.

## Understanding Membership Rules

Membership rules are access control settings that determine which content your members can view based on their membership level. When a visitor without the required membership tries to access restricted content, they'll see a restriction message instead.

Here's a quick overview of how membership rules work:

Feature
Details

**Rules per membership**
Each membership plan can have exactly one membership rule

**Content targeting**
Restrict entire sites, specific pages, posts, custom post types, menu items, files, or URLs

**Access enforcement**
Access is granted or denied automatically based on the member's active subscription

**Centralized management**
View and manage all rules from **User Registration & Membership → Content Rules → Membership Rules**

## Creating a Membership Rule

You can create a membership rule in two ways: directly from the membership plan editor, or from the Content Rules dashboard.

### Method 1: From the Membership Plan Editor

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Memberships** from your WordPress dashboard.

Click **Edit** on an existing membership plan, or click **Add New** to create one.

In the membership editor, click the **Access** tab at the top of the page.

Click the **Content** dropdown and select the type of content you want to restrict (see the Content Types section below for all available options).

After selecting a content type, choose the specific items you want to include in the rule. For example, if you selected **Selected Pages**, a list of your site's pages will appear — choose which ones to restrict.

Click **Save Changes** to apply the membership rule.

### Method 2: From the Content Rules Dashboard

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Content Rules** and click the **Membership Rules** tab.

Click **Add Rule**.

Select the membership plan this rule applies to.

Configure the rule using the content selection options described below.

Click **Save** to create the membership rule.

Both methods create the same rule. Changes made in either location are reflected in the other — they are two different views of the same setting.

## Content Types

When setting up a membership rule, the **Content** dropdown lets you choose what type of content to restrict. Here's what each option does:

Content Type
Description
Availability

**Whole Site**
Grants or restricts access to your entire website
Free & Pro

**Selected Pages**
Restricts access to specific pages you choose
Free & Pro

**Specific Posts**
Controls access to individual posts
Free & Pro

**Custom Post Types**
Restricts content from custom post types (e.g., portfolios, products)
Pro only

**Menu Items**
Controls the visibility of specific navigation menu items
Pro only

**Taxonomies**
Restricts content based on categories, tags, or custom taxonomies
Pro only

**Custom URI**
Restricts access to specific URL patterns
Pro only

**File Downloads**
Controls file access (requires the File Downloads add-on)
Pro only

## Configuring the Restriction Message

When a visitor tries to access restricted content without the required membership, they'll see a restriction message. You can customize this message to explain your membership benefits or encourage visitors to sign up.

**To set a global restriction message:**

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Content Restriction**.

In the **Restricted Content Message** field, enter the message you want to display to non-members.

Use the **Add Media** button to include images if needed. The field also supports smart tags, formatting, and links.

Click **Save Changes**.

If you leave the Restricted Content Message field empty, the plugin will display a default fallback message automatically.

You can also override the global message for a specific membership rule by configuring a custom restriction message within that rule's settings.

## Managing Existing Membership Rules

To view all your membership rules, go to **User Registration & Membership → Content Rules → Membership Rules**. Here, you'll see a list of all rules organized by membership plan.

**To edit a rule:** Click the rule name or click **Edit** in the rule's action menu. You can update the content selection, restriction message, or any other setting.

**To temporarily disable a rule:** Toggle the **Status** switch to off. The rule will remain saved but won't be enforced until you re-enable it. This is useful for testing or pausing access restrictions without permanently removing them.

**To delete a rule:** Click **Delete** in the rule's action menu. This action cannot be undone.

## Membership Rules vs. Custom Rules

User Registration & Membership offers two types of content restriction rules. Understanding the difference helps you choose the right tool for each scenario.

Membership Rules
Custom Rules

**Tied to a membership plan**
Yes — one rule per plan
No — standalone rules

**Condition types**
Membership-based only
Advanced: user roles, registration dates, email domains, and more

**Logic operators**
Not applicable
AND / OR / NOT logic supported

**Availability**
Free & Pro
Pro only

**Best for**
Straightforward members-only content protection
Complex, multi-condition access control

For most membership sites, membership rules provide everything you need to protect premium content and manage member access effectively.

Custom rules are evaluated alongside membership rules and **can override** membership rules when conditions are met. If a custom rule grants or denies access to the same content, it takes precedence. This allows for more granular control when needed.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I create multiple membership rules for one membership plan?

No. Each membership plan can have only one membership rule. However, a single rule can restrict multiple types of content at once — for example, specific pages, posts, and menu items can all be included in the same rule.

### What happens if a user has multiple active memberships?

If a user holds more than one active membership, they'll have access to all content allowed by any of their membership plans. Access permissions are additive — having multiple memberships only expands what a user can access, never reduces it.

### Can the same content be restricted to multiple membership plans?

Yes. To make a piece of content accessible to multiple membership plans, create a separate membership rule for each plan that includes that content. Users with any of those plans will then be able to access it.

## Next Steps

After setting up your membership rules, you may want to explore **Custom Rules** for more advanced access control scenarios — including conditions based on user roles, registration dates, email domains, and complex logic. Custom Rules are available in the **Pro** plan and can complement or override your membership rules for greater flexibility.

👉 Learn more about Content Rules in User Registration & Membership Pro

## Subscription Upgrade Path in Memberships

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/subscription-upgrade-path>

Set Up Membership Upgrade Paths with Proration | URM Docs

# Subscription Upgrade Path in Memberships
Learn how to configure membership tier upgrade paths with automatic proration, allowing members to switch plans while crediting their remaining subscription time.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Would you like to let your members switch between membership tiers without losing their investment?

User Registration & Membership allows you to create upgrade paths that let members move from one plan to another—with automatic proration that credits their remaining time. This tutorial will show you how to set up membership upgrade paths and manage the upgrade process.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership plugin on your WordPress site. Then, make sure you've created at least two membership plans that you want to connect with an upgrade path.

## Understanding Upgrade Paths

An upgrade path defines which membership plans your members can switch to from their current plan. When you enable upgrade paths, members see a **Change Plan** button in their account dashboard that lets them move to a different tier.

User Registration & Membership supports two upgrade pricing models(for subscriptions):

**Full Amount Upgrade** — Members pay the complete price of the new membership plan

**Proration Upgrade** — Members pay only the difference based on their remaining subscription time

Proration Upgrade requires User Registration & Membership Pro v5.3.0 or higher.

## Enabling Upgrade Action for a Membership Plan (Pro)

To make a membership plan upgradeable, you'll configure its upgrade settings in the membership editor.

From your WordPress dashboard, go to **User Registration & Membership → Memberships**. Here, you'll see a list of all your membership plans.

Click **Edit** on the membership plan you want to make upgradeable. This opens the membership editor where you can configure all plan settings.

Click on the **Advanced tab**. Here, you'll find the upgrade configuration options.

Toggle the **Upgrade Action** switch to enable upgrade functionality for this plan. Once enabled, additional upgrade settings will appear below.

## Selecting the Upgrade Path

Once Upgrade Action is enabled, you'll see the **Upgrade Path** field. This field determines which membership plans members can upgrade to from the current plan.

Click in the **Upgrade Path** field. A dropdown appears showing all your available membership plans. Select one or more plans that you want members to be able to upgrade to.

For example, if you're editing a Basic plan, you might select Gold and Diamond plans as upgrade options. Members on the Basic plan will then see both Silver and Gold as available upgrades. Or, just **Diamond **like this screenshot and user will be upgraded to Diamond from Basic plan.

You can select multiple upgrade options to give members flexibility in choosing their next tier.

Design your upgrade paths to make sense for your members:

**Linear Progression:**

Basic → Premium → Professional

Each tier builds upon the previous with additional features

**Flexible Options:**

Basic → Premium OR Professional

Allow members to choose the upgrade that best fits their needs

## Choosing the Upgrade Pricing Model

After selecting your upgrade path, choose how upgrade pricing will be calculated.

User Registration & Membership offers two pricing models:

**Full Amount Upgrade** — Members pay the complete price of the new membership plan. This is the simpler option and works for all membership types, including upgrades from free plans to paid plans.

**Proration Upgrade** — Members pay only the difference based on their remaining subscription time. The system automatically calculates how much of their current subscription they've used, credits the unused portion, and charges only the difference for the new plan.

The proration formula works like this:

Text JavaScript TypeScript JSX TSX JSON PHP Python Bash HTML CSS SCSS SQL YAML Markdown Go Java Ruby Rust
`final_price = upgrade_price - (initial_paid_price - (price_per_day × days_passed))`

Here's what each part means:

**Days Used** — How many days have passed since the member started their current subscription

**Daily Rate** — The daily cost of their current plan (total price ÷ subscription days)

**Remaining Credit** — The value of unused time on their current plan

**Final Price** — What the member pays for the upgrade

Proration only applies to paid subscription plans. Upgrades from free plans always use the full amount pricing model.

Click **Save** to save your upgrade configuration.

Before members can upgrade, you need to ensure your payment gateways are properly configured.

## Testing the Upgrade Flow

Before going live, test your upgrade path using sandbox or test mode.

Create a test member account and purchase the base membership plan using test payment credentials. Log in as that test member and navigate to the **Membership** tab in their account dashboard.

You should see the **Change Plan** button next to the current membership. Click it to view available upgrade options.

Select an upgrade option from the pop-up. The system displays the upgrade price based on your pricing model (full amount or prorated).

Choose a payment gateway and complete the test payment. For PayPal, you'll be redirected to PayPal's sandbox site. For Stripe, you can enter test card details directly.

After successful payment, verify that the member's account immediately reflects the new membership tier and that they have access to the upgraded content.

## How Members Upgrade Their Membership

Once you've configured upgrade paths, here's how the upgrade process works for your members.

Members log into their account and click the **Membership** tab in their account dashboard. They see their current membership plan with a **Change Plan** button.

When they click **Change Plan**, a pop-up appears showing all available upgrade options you've configured in the upgrade path.

Members select their desired upgrade option. The system displays the upgrade price - either the full amount or the prorated amount based on your configuration.

Members choose their preferred payment gateway from the available options (Stripe, PayPal, Bank Transfer, etc.).

For PayPal, members are redirected to PayPal to complete payment. For Stripe, they enter their card details directly on your site. For bank transfer, they receive instructions for making the payment.

After successful payment, the member's account updates immediately. They gain access to all content and features included in their new membership tier.

If a member chooses bank transfer, you'll need to manually approve the payment from the **Payment History** tab before their upgrade takes effect.

## Understanding Upgrade vs. Downgrade Behavior

User Registration & Membership handles upgrades and downgrades differently based on the membership type.

**Upgrades from subscription plans** — When a member upgrades from a recurring subscription to a higher-tier subscription, the change happens immediately after payment. Their billing cycle adjusts to the new plan's schedule.

**Downgrades from subscription plans** — When a member downgrades to a lower-tier subscription, the change is delayed until their current subscription expires. This ensures they receive the full value of what they've already paid for.

**Downgrades from one-time payment plans** — When a member downgrades from a one-time payment plan to either a free plan or a subscription plan, the change happens immediately.

**Upgrades from free plans** — Upgrades from free memberships always use full amount pricing, since there's no previous payment to prorate.

## Common Upgrade Scenarios

Here are some common upgrade path configurations and how they work:

**Three-tier membership (Bronze → Silver → Gold)** — Set Bronze to upgrade to Silver and Gold. Set Silver to upgrade to Gold only. Gold has no upgrade path since it's the top tier.

**Freemium model (Free → Premium)** — Set the free plan to upgrade to one or more paid plans. Use full amount pricing since there's no previous payment to prorate.

**Flexible upgrades** — Allow members to upgrade to multiple options at once. For example, a Basic plan might offer upgrades to both a Premium plan and a Premium Plus plan, giving members choice.

**Subscription to lifetime** — Set a monthly or yearly subscription to upgrade to a lifetime access plan. Members pay once and never renew again.

## Team Management

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/team-management>

Team Management | User Registration & Membership Docs

# Team Management
Pro Configure team-based memberships with custom pricing tiers, assign team leaders, and manage multi-user access for group subscriptions.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

Want to let one person purchase access for multiple users? User Registration & Membership includes team management tools to help you create team pricing, assign team leaders, and manage members. This guide shows you how to manage teams on your membership site.

Before getting started, make sure you've installed and activated the User Registration & Membership Pro plugin with a Plus or Professional plan license. Then, make sure you've activated the Team Membership addon and created at least one membership plan with team pricing enabled.

## **Setting Team Pricing in Membership**

Team pricing allows you to define how much a team is charged based on the number of seats and the selected pricing model.

#### **Step 1: Create or Edit a Membership**

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Memberships**.

Create a new membership plan or edit an existing one.

Enable the **Team Pricing** option for the selected plan.

#### **Step 2: Configure Your First Pricing Tier**

Enter a **Team Name** (e.g., "Small Team" or "Enterprise")

Select your **Seat Model**:

**Fixed Seats:** Specify an exact number of seats (e.g., 10)

**Variable Seats:** Define minimum and maximum seat limits (e.g., 5-50)

If you selected **Fixed Seats**, enter the total team price (a single price for the entire team).

If you selected **Variable Seats**, choose your **Pricing Model**:

**Per Seat:** Set a price per individual seat

**Tiered Pricing:** Create multiple price tiers based on seat ranges (e.g., 1–5, 6–10, 11–25 seats) and assign a price per seat to each tier. Click the "**Add Tier**" button to add additional ranges.

Select your **Pricing Type**:

**One-time PaymentSubscription-Based** (monthly, yearly, etc.)To create additional pricing tiers, click the "**Add Another Team Pricing**" button.

#### **Step 3: Save Your Membership**

Click **Publish **button at the top right corner to save your team pricing configuration.

## **Team Membership Display in Registration Form**

The registration form initially displays **regular (individual) membership pricing** for all memberships. When a user selects **Team Membership**, the form dynamically updates to show team-specific pricing options, including:

**All available pricing tiers** displayed as cards/options

**Team name, team size/seat range and pricing details with duration** clearly shown

**Seat Input** field that allows users to enter the number of seats they want to purchase for the team within the allowed seat range (for variable seats)

**Tier Selection** option for tier-based pricing

Users first select a tier (seat range)

The seat input is restricted to the selected tier’s range

**Real-time price calculation** as users select or change seats

## Accessing the Teams Dashboard

To view and manage your teams, go to **User Registration & Membership → Teams** from your WordPress admin dashboard. Here, you'll see a comprehensive list of all teams that have been created through team membership purchases.

The Teams dashboard displays key information including team names, assigned team leaders, and the number of team members in each team. This gives you a quick overview of all team activity on your site.

## Understanding Team Information

Each team entry in the dashboard shows:

Team Name: The display name for the team

Team Leader: The user assigned to manage the team

Team Members: The number of active members in the team

Team leaders are the users who purchased the team membership and have permission to add or remove team members within their allocated seat limit.

## **Managing Teams (Admin)**

Navigate to **User Registration & Membership → Teams** to manage team settings. You will see a list of teams along with the assigned team leader and the number of team members in each team.

### **Edit Team Details**

To edit a team, hover over a team row and click **Edit **button. Admin can update the following team details:

**Team Name** – Enter a new team name.

**Team Leader** – Assign or change the team leader.

**Team Seats** – Update the total number of seats allocated to the team.

**Team Members** – Add or remove team members

### **Changing Team Leader**

Admin can change the team leader from the team edit form. In the **Team Leader** field, select a new leader from the dropdown of registered users.

### **Managing Team Members**

Admin can manage team members directly from the team edit form.

**Add MembersExisting Users: **Add registered users to the team by selecting them from the **Members **dropdown.

**New users:** Type the email in **Members **field. The Add new email option will appear and click it to add the user. An email is sent automatically with their login credentials and a reset password link.

**Remove Members**

Remove users from the team by clicking the **X **button on the email tag.

**View Member Details**

See team members information including User ID, email, name, role, and status below the edit form.

After adding/removing team members, changing the team leader or updating team details, click the **Update** button in the top right corner to save your changes.

#### **Important Notes**

Each email must be **valid** (validated automatically).

Cannot add **duplicate emails**.

Maximum members are **limited by the purchased seat count**.

Members are **directly added to the team**.

Changing the team leader does not remove them from the team members list.

## **Team Leader Account Page**

When a user purchases a team membership, they become the **team leader** and gain access to team management through their account page.

### **Accessing Team Page**

Team leaders can access their teams management from:

Log into their account

Navigate to **My Account → Team **from the sidebar menu

View all teams they’ve created/purchased

The Team menu item only appears for users who have purchased at least one team membership.

### **Updating Team Details**

To edit a team, Team Leaders can do the following:

**If the user has only one team**: Clicking the **Team** tab in the sidebar will directly open the edit form.

**If the user has multiple teams**: Clicking the **Team** tab will display a table of teams. Click the **Edit** button for the desired team to open the edit form.

#### **Editable FieldsTeam Name** (required) – Give your team a meaningful name

**Members List** – Add or remove member emails

### **Managing Team Members**

Team Leaders can manage team members directly from the team edit form.

**Add Members**

Enter the email in the **Members **section and click the **+** button. An email is sent automatically with their login credentials and a reset password link after updating the team.

**Remove Members**

Click the **Remove **button of each user on the members list section to remove them from the team.

**View Member Details**

See team members information including email, name, and status in the **Members List **section.

After adding/removing team members or updating team details, click the **Update** button to save the changes.

## **Email Notifications**

You can customize team-related emails from **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Emails → To User**.

Team Registration Success Email: Sent when someone joins a team

Team Member Reset Password Email: Sent **only when a new user** (not already registered) is added to the team.

## Frequently Asked Questions

These are answers to some of the most common questions we receive about team management.

### Can I add more members than the purchased seat count?

No. The maximum number of members is limited by the purchased seat count. You must increase the team seats before adding additional members.

### What happens when I change the team leader?

The new team leader gains access to team management through their My Account page. The previous team leader loses management access but remains a team member unless you manually remove them.

### Can I add the same email to multiple teams?

No. Each email address must be unique within a team. However, a user can be a member of multiple different teams.

### Do team members need to confirm their email?

Only users with confirmed email addresses will show in the team members list. New users added to a team receive an email with login credentials and must verify their email if email confirmation is enabled in your form settings.

That's it! Now you know how to manage teams in User Registration & Membership. Next, would you like to learn how to set up team pricing for your membership plans? Be sure to check out our guide on configuring team membership pricing for all the details.

## Team Membership

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/membership/team-membership>

Team Membership | User Registration & Membership Docs

# Team Membership
Pro Sell and manage group memberships with centralized billing, allowing organizations to provide shared access to multiple team members under one subscription.
Last updated on Jul 15, 2026

The Team Membership add-on enables you to sell and manage memberships for teams rather than individual users. This feature is ideal for businesses, agencies, schools, or organizations that need to provide shared access to multiple members under a single subscription with centralized billing and management.

## **Before You Begin**

Ensure you have:

User Registration & Membership Pro installed and activated with a valid license key

A Plus or Professional plan (Team Membership is not available on basic plans)

At least one membership plan created (or be ready to create one)

## **Activate the Team Membership Add-on**

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Addons** in your WordPress dashboard

Locate **Team Membership** in the add-ons list (you can use the search field if needed)

Toggle the switch to **Activate** the add-on

The add-on is now active and ready to use.

## **Configure Team Pricing for a Membership**

Team pricing determines how much a team is charged based on the number of seats and your chosen pricing model.

### **Step 1: Create or Edit a Membership Plan**

Navigate to **User Registration & Membership → Memberships**

Click **Create new Membership** to create a new plan, or click **Edit** on an existing membership

Locate the **Team Pricing** option in the membership settings

Toggle **Enable Team Pricing** to activate team membership for this plan

### **Step 2: Create Your First Pricing Tier**

A pricing tier defines how many seats are available and how much the team will pay.

Enter a **Team Name** (e.g., "Small Team," "Enterprise Team," "Starter Package")

Choose your **Seat Model**:

**Fixed Seats**: Enter a specific number of seats (e.g., 10 seats). The team size is locked to this number.

**Variable Seats**: Enter a minimum and maximum seat range (e.g., 5–50 seats). Buyers can choose how many seats they need within this range.

#### Configure pricing based on your seat model:

**If you chose Fixed Seats:**

Enter a single **Team Price** (e.g., $200 for 10 seats)

**If you chose Variable Seats:**

Select a **Pricing Model**:

**Per Seat Pricing**: Enter a price per seat (e.g., $20 per seat). Total cost = seats × price per seat.

**Tiered Pricing**: Create multiple price tiers based on seat ranges. For example:

1–5 seats: $25 per seat

6–10 seats: $20 per seat

11–25 seats: $15 per seat

Click **Add Tier** to add additional pricing tiers

#### Choose your **Pricing Type**:

**One-time payment**: Team pays once for lifetime access

**Subscription Based**: Recurring payments (monthly, yearly, or custom intervals)

To create multiple team pricing tiers for the same membership (e.g., Small Team, Medium Team, Enterprise Team), click **Add Another Team Pricing** and repeat the configuration.

### **Step 3: Save Your Membership**

Click the **Publish** button in the top right corner to save your team pricing configuration

Your team membership is now live and ready for purchase.

## **How Team Membership Appears on Registration Forms**

When users visit your registration form, they will initially see individual membership pricing for all available plans. When a user selects a membership configured with team pricing, the form dynamically updates to display:

**All available pricing tiers** displayed as selectable cards or options

**Team name, seat range, and pricing details** with subscription duration clearly shown

**Seat input field** (for variable seats) allowing users to enter the number of seats they want to purchase within the allowed range

**Tier selection option** (for tiered pricing) where users first select a tier, then the seat input is restricted to that tier's range

**Real-time price calculation** that updates as users select or change the number of seats

Users complete the registration form, select their desired team size, and proceed to payment. Upon successful payment, they become the team leader.

## **Managing Teams (Admin)**

As an administrator, you have full control over all teams created on your site.

### **Access the Teams Dashboard**

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Teams** in your WordPress dashboard

You will see a list of all teams with the following information:

Team name

Assigned team leader

Number of team members

### **Edit Team Details**

Hover over the team row you want to edit

Click the **Edit** button

You can update the following:

**Team Name**: Enter a new name for the team

**Team Leader**: Assign or change the team leader by selecting a user from the dropdown

**Team Seats**: Update the total number of seats allocated to the team

**Team Members**: Add or remove team members (see below)

### **Change the Team Leader**

In the team edit form, locate the **Team Leader** field

Click the dropdown and select a new team leader from the list of registered users

Click **Update** in the top right corner to save the change

Changing the team leader does not remove the previous leader from the team members list. They remain a member unless manually removed.

### **Add Team Members**

You can add existing users or invite new users to the team.

**To add an existing user:**

In the **Members** field, click the dropdown

Select the user from the list of registered users

The user is added to the team immediately

**To invite a new user:**

In the **Members** field, type the email address of the new user

An **Add new email** option will appear

Click the option to add the user

An email is sent automatically to the new user with their login credentials and a password reset link

### **Remove Team Members**

In the **Members** field, locate the user you want to remove

Click the **X** button on the email tag

The user is removed from the team

### **View Member Details**

Below the edit form, you can view detailed information about each team member, including:

User ID

Email address

Name

User role

Account status

After making any changes to team details, team leader, or team members, click the **Update** button in the top right corner. Your changes are saved and applied immediately.

## **Team Leader Account Page**

When a user purchases a team membership, they automatically become the team leader and gain access to team management tools through their account page.

### **Access the Team Management Page**

Log into your account on the website

Navigate to **My Account → Team** from the sidebar menu

You will see all teams you have created or purchased

The Team menu item only appears for users who have purchased at least one team membership.

### **Edit Team DetailsIf you have only one team:**

Clicking the **Team** tab in the sidebar will directly open the team edit form

**If you have multiple teams:**

Clicking the **Team** tab will display a table listing all your teams

Click the **Edit** button for the team you want to manage

Team leaders can update the following:

**Team Name** (required): Give your team a meaningful name

**Members List**: Add or remove member email addresses

### **Add Team Members**

In the **Members** section, enter the email address of the person you want to add

Click the **+** button

The member is added to the team

An email is sent automatically to the new member with their login credentials and a password reset link after you update the team

### **Remove Team Members**

In the **Members List** section, locate the member you want to remove

Click the **Remove** button next to their name

The member is removed from the team

### **View Member Details**

In the **Members List** section, you can view information about each team member, including:

Email address

Name

Account status

After adding or removing team members or updating team details, click the **Update** button. Your changes are saved and team members are notified as needed.

## **Email Notifications**

The Team Membership add-on sends automated emails to team members at key moments. You can customize these email templates to match your branding and communication style.

You can customize team-related emails from **User Registration & Membership → Settings → Emails → To User**.

Team Registration Success Email: Sent when someone joins a team

Team Member Reset Password Email: Sent **only when a new user** (not already registered) is added to the team.
